analysis.title: The 720: Tencent, 2027 Outlooks: Global Credit & India Strategy, Nvidia, Broadcom, APAC DCs, Panasonic, Miniso, China Basic Materials
key_insights: Tencent 3Q26 revenue grew 8% YoY and operating profit fell 6%, missing GSe by 2 ppt and 6 ppt on softer international games and elevated AI spending. GS cuts 4Q26E, FY27E and FY28E adjusted net profit by 5%, 11% and 11% and lowers the 12m TP to HK$610 from HK$650 (Buy).

Tencent management expects capex intensity to peak as compute prepayments decline now that long-term contracts are secured. Cloud revenue growth accelerated to 35% YoY on new AI products and advertising grew 19% YoY. GS sees FY27E as the likely EPS trough.

2027 Global Credit Outlook: GS expects modest spread widening across USD and EUR IG and HY, a three-speed market split by an AI divide, and a shift to IG over HY in USD. It stays neutral on EUR, favors BBBs over higher-quality cohorts because of AI-related debt at AAA and AA issuers, and is underweight USD HY Technology.

GS forecasts default rates rising modestly to 4% for USD HY and 5% for EUR HY. Key overweights remain Banks, Energy and Health Care, and GS prefers picking up subordination premium over moving down in credit quality.

India upgraded to overweight with an end-2027 NIFTY target of 28,500, after 83 ppt of peak-to-trough underperformance versus MXAPJ from mid-2024 to late-2026. GS forecasts NIFTY EPS growth of 15% in both CY27 and CY28 and real GDP growth of 7.2% in CY27E versus 7.9% in CY26E.

India sector calls: Industrials upgraded to overweight on a nascent private capex recovery. GS also prefers Banks, Defense, Utilities, Telcos and Internet, and underweights IT, Healthcare, Metals, and Cement and Chemicals.

ASEAN macro 2027: AI-related exports and investment keep growth firm in Malaysia (4.8%) and Singapore (3.2%) and lift Thailand to 2.3%. Indonesia slows to 5.0% as fiscal support fades and the Philippines recovers to 4.0%. GS expects Singapore, Thailand and the Philippines to hold rates, Malaysia to hike 25bps to 3% in 1Q27 and Indonesia to reach 6.25% by 1Q27.

Nvidia 3Q26 revenue of $115.8bn and operating EPS of $2.68 beat GS and consensus. 4Q26 revenue guidance is $130bn at the midpoint, ahead of the Street, and management raised its CY27 revenue growth forecast to 75% on Blackwell, Rubin, Vera and Groq demand. GS raises EPS estimates by an average of 4% (Buy, 12m TP $220).

Nvidia says unconstrained CY27 demand growth is well in excess of supply, with commitments to customers and supply chain partners now totaling $518bn. It intends to complete its remaining $227bn buyback authorization before the end of CY27. GS flags ongoing investigations and the management transition as heightened risks.

Broadcom 3Q preview: GS expects modest upside to guidance and lowers its 12m TP to $460 from $540. Its FY27 and FY28 AI revenue estimates are 5% and 9% above consensus and EPS estimates 5% and 12% above, and it believes expectations are muted. Focus items are AI spending sustainability into 2028 given land, power and shell constraints, custom XPU deployments to emerging hyperscalers, and competition from MediaTek at Google.

The US BIS interim final rule on remote access to advanced semiconductors shifts regulation toward compute access. GS sees demand reallocation, not structural impairment, for ASEAN data centers. China-linked AI workloads are an estimated 0.5-0.75GW, or 15-25% of ASEAN live data center demand, and China-heavy training projects in Malaysia face higher leasing risk.

Panasonic HD CEO meeting: management keeps flexible production for battery backup units supplied to US hyperscalers and plans further capacity expansion for capacitors and CCLs supplied to Chinese data centers. AI-related battery capacity investment is almost complete. Panasonic Electric Works profitability improved on price revisions and CRM data use (Buy, 12m TP ¥6,300).

China Basic Materials Monitor: end-user orderbooks recovered in mid-November after a weak October, but metal price volatility caused the first pushback in months. First-half November demand was 2-10% lower YoY for cement and steel and 2% higher for copper and aluminium. Copper scrap disruptions persist, lithium supply eased, and margins softened for aluminium, copper, lithium and steel.

CSPC Pharma 3Q26 beat on CNS momentum and operating leverage. Revenue of Rmb6.7bn grew 0.7% YoY, finished drug sales rose 10% versus GS's 6% estimate with CNS up 32%, while API sales fell 23.8%. Management guides to positive finished-drug sales growth in 2027 (Buy, 12m TP HK$12.83).

JD Group 3Q26 results were broadly in line, but GS sees a weaker 4Q setup from soft consumption and AI-related R&D costs that management expects to peak in 4Q26. Management targets halving food delivery losses in 2027 and JD Industrials revenue grew 36% YoY (Buy, JD TPs US$43/HK$169, JD Industrials HK$17.9 unchanged).

India Metals & Mining Q2FY27: EBITDA/t largely surpassed GS and consensus estimates on lower coking coal costs and better product mix. GS expects stronger H2FY27 on 6-6.5% YoY domestic steel consumption growth and spot spreads near four-year highs. Preferred Buys are JSW Steel (on CL), Jindal Stainless and Shyam Metalics.

Miniso CFO meeting: China revenue and profit momentum is healthy in 4Q, while overseas DTC growth may moderate as store openings slow. Management plans to cut US pop toy markups, run selective 4Q promotions to clear overseas inventory and move to regional management in 2027 (Buy, 12m TPs US$16/HK$31.12).

China banks (small and medium): the deposit repricing benefit is likely to moderate into 2027, shifting earnings differentiation to asset-side execution. NIM pressure is easing, corporate lending drives growth and retail demand is softer. Bank of Nanjing is Neutral and Industrial Bank is Sell.

China is reportedly assessing removal of the corporate income tax exemption on central and local government bond interest. GS estimates a 10-30bps yield premium on newly taxable 10-year bonds, with initial repricing toward the upper bound, and expects bear-steepening pressure. Weak growth and inflation still support long-dated government bonds.

Bank Indonesia surprised with a 25bp hike to 6% against GS and consensus expectations for no change, citing Fed tightening risk and rupiah weakness with USDIDR above 18,200. It raised DNDF hedging discounts and will add a cross-currency repo facility by March 2027. GS still expects one more 25bps hike in 1Q27 to 6.25%.

ASML management meeting: High NA momentum is strong, with 90% fleet availability targeted and 13 tools running by year-end. GS considers Match Act concerns overdone and expects no meaningful impact on DUV shipments to China before 2028 (Buy on CL, 12m TP €2,315).

Nike investor day FY31 framework targets about $5bn of incremental revenue from the FY27 base, a 12%-14% adjusted operating margin and $3.00-$3.50 of adjusted EPS. FY27 and FY28 remain investment years with FY28 EPS projected down YoY and below prior consensus. GS sees elevated execution risk (Neutral, 12m TP $30).

Carbonomics: GS estimates solar geo-engineering is cheaper than decarbonization per degree of cooling. SAI and MCB could deliver equivalent cooling for 7% and 10% of the cost of decarbonization investment, with SAI at US$60-70bn annually per 1°C of avoided warming. Main drawback is the risk of unpredictable weather and precipitation changes.
A graphic in the Global Credit Outlook shows GS expects $440 billion of direct hyperscaler issuance and $545 billion of AI-related project finance debt in 2027.

risk_factors: AI infrastructure spending sustainability into 2028 given land, power and shell constraints, and external funding concerns for emerging hyperscalers.
Tencent elevated AI spending, content costs and elevated memory prices pressuring near-term margins.
Leasing risk for China-customer-heavy training data center projects in Malaysia under the US BIS rule.
Food price risks from El Niño and elevated fertilizer costs may temper disinflation in ASEAN.
Heavy AI-related debt issuance by AAA and AA issuers, with $440 billion of hyperscaler issuance expected in 2027.
Execution risk at Nike as new products launch and scale, and at Miniso in overseas markets.
Metal price volatility pushing back end-user orderbooks in China.

vol_and_positioning: India foreign positioning is at decade lows, supporting GS's mean-reversion case for an overweight.
Broadcom expectations are described as muted as investors reassess the durability of AI infrastructure spending.
geopolitical: US BIS interim final rule on remote access to advanced semiconductors introduces license requirements for facilities providing over 12mn TPP to China-linked entities and destination license requirements for advanced chip shipments.
Match Act proposals could restrict DUV shipments to China, with GS expecting no meaningful impact before 2028 as it hinges on implementation in other jurisdictions.
China is reportedly assessing removal of the tax exemption on government bond interest.
Ongoing investigations and a management transition at Nvidia are cited as heightened risks.
